translations.literal: Eleventh month, day gengwu: an edict—only men without examination origin who had reached vice drafter or above, were thirty or older, and had served ten full years in office might confer office on sons.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month, gengwu: only men without examination origin who had reached vice drafter, were thirty or older, and had served ten full years might confer office on sons.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，遣使回慶金國。

translations.literal: Day yihai: envoys were sent to return congratulations to the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, envoys were sent to return congratulations to the Jin.

sentences.zh: 甲申，朝獻景靈宮。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: the Jingling Palace was presented in court audience.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the Jingling Palace was presented in court audience.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，饗太廟。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: the Ancestral Temple was feasted.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, the Ancestral Temple was feasted.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，祀昊天上帝於圜丘，赦天下。

translations.literal: Day bingxu: the Supreme Lord was sacrificed to at the Round Mound; the realm was amnestied.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, Heaven was sacrificed to at the Round Mound and the realm amnestied.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以保靜軍節度使種師道為河東、河北路制置使。

translations.literal: Day gengyin: Baojing Army military commissioner Zhong Shidao was made commissioner-general of Hebei and Hedong circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Baojing commissioner Zhong Shidao became commissioner-general of Hebei and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 十二月乙巳，童貫自太原遁歸京師。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day yisi: Tong Guan fled from Taiyuan back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, yisi: Tong Guan fled from Taiyuan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 己酉，中山奏金人斡離不、粘罕分兩道入攻。

translations.literal: Day jiyou: Zhongshan reported Jin commanders Wolibu and Nianhan advancing in two columns.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Zhongshan reported Jin commanders Wolibu and Nianhan advancing in two columns.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師以燕山叛，北邊諸郡皆陷。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi rebelled with the Yan Mountains; northern border prefectures all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi rebelled with the Yan Mountains and northern border prefectures fell.

sentences.zh: 又陷忻、代等州，圍太原府。

translations.literal: Xin and Dai prefectures also fell; Taiyuan prefecture was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Xin and Dai also fell and Taiyuan was besieged.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿傅察奉使不屈，死之。

translations.literal: Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice minister Fu Cha went on embassy and would not yield; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Imperial Sacrifices vice minister Fu Cha went on embassy, would not yield, and died.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，罷浙江諸路花石綱、延福宮、西城租課及內外製造局。

translations.literal: Day bingchen: the Zhejiang Flower-and-Stone convoys, Yanfu Palace, Xicheng rent levies, and inner and outer manufacture offices were all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Zhejiang Flower-and-Stone convoys, Yanfu Palace, Xicheng rents, and inner and outer manufacture offices were abolished.

sentences.zh: 金兵犯中山府，詹度禦之。

translations.literal: Jin troops attacked Zhongshan prefecture; Zhan Du defended it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin troops attacked Zhongshan; Zhan Du defended it.

sentences.zh: 戊午，皇太子桓為開封牧。

translations.literal: Day wuwu: the heir apparent Huan was made Kaifeng intendant.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, heir apparent Huan became Kaifeng intendant.

sentences.zh: 罷修蕃衍北宅，令諸皇子分居十位。

translations.literal: Construction of the Fanxing North Residence was halted; the various princes were ordered to live separately in the ten residences.
translations.idiomatic: Fanxing North Residence construction was halted and the princes were ordered to live separately in ten residences.

sentences.zh: 己未，下詔罪己。

translations.literal: Day jiwei: a self-reproach edict was issued.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, a self-reproach edict was issued.

sentences.zh: 令中外直言極諫，郡邑率師勤王，募草澤異才有能出奇計及使疆外者。

translations.literal: Court and provinces were ordered to speak bluntly in utmost remonstrance; prefectures were to lead troops to aid the throne; commoners of unusual talent who could offer stratagems or serve beyond the borders were to be recruited.
translations.idiomatic: Court and provinces were told to remonstrate bluntly; prefectures were to lead troops to aid the throne; and men of talent who could offer stratagems or serve beyond the borders were to be recruited.

sentences.zh: 罷道官，罷大晟府、行幸局。

translations.literal: Daoist offices were abolished, as were the Great Splendor Bureau and the Imperial Progress Office.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist offices, the Great Splendor Bureau, and the Imperial Progress Office were abolished.

sentences.zh: 西城及諸局所管緡錢，盡付有司。

translations.literal: String-cash of Xicheng and the various offices were all handed over to the regular authorities.
translations.idiomatic: Xicheng and the various offices’ string-cash were handed to the regular authorities.

sentences.zh: 以保和殿大學士宇文虛中為河北、河東路宣諭使。

translations.literal: Baohé Hall university scholar Yuwen Xuzhong was made pacification and instruction commissioner of Hebei and Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Baohé Hall scholar Yuwen Xuzhong became pacification commissioner of Hebei and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 庚申，詔內禪，皇太子即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Day gengshen: an edict ordered inner abdication; the heir apparent took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen, inner abdication was ordered and the heir apparent took the throne.

sentences.zh: 尊帝為教主道君太上皇帝，居於龍德宮。

translations.literal: The emperor was honored as Retired Emperor, Patriarch and Sovereign of the Way, and dwelt at Longde Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was honored Retired Emperor, Patriarch and Sovereign of the Way, and dwelt at Longde Palace.

sentences.zh: 尊皇后為太上皇后。

translations.literal: The empress was honored as Retired Empress.
translations.idiomatic: The empress was honored Retired Empress.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年正月己巳，詣亳州太清宮，行恭謝禮，遂幸鎮江府。

translations.literal: Jingkang year 1, first month, day jisi: he went to the Grand Pure Palace at Bozhou, performed the thanksgiving rite, and then proceeded to Zhenjiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jingkang 1, jisi: he went to Bozhou’s Grand Pure Palace for thanksgiving, then proceeded to Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 四月己亥，還京師。

translations.literal: Fourth month, day jihai: he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month, jihai: he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 明年二月丁卯，金人脅帝北行。

translations.literal: The next year, second month, day dingmao: Jin forced the emperor north.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, second month, dingmao: the Jin forced the emperor north.

sentences.zh: 紹興五年四月甲子，崩于五國城，年五十有四。

translations.literal: Shaoxing year 5, fourth month, day jiazi: he died at Wuguo City, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 5, fourth month, jiazi: he died at Wuguo City, aged fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 七年九月甲子，凶問至江南，遙上尊諡曰聖文仁德顯孝皇帝，廟號徽宗。

translations.literal: Year 7, ninth month, day jiazi: word of his death reached the south; from afar the honorific Sagely Culture, Humaneness, Virtue, and Manifest Filiality Emperor was conferred; temple name Huizong.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7, ninth month, jiazi: word of his death reached the south; from afar he received the honorific Sagely Culture, Humaneness, Virtue, and Manifest Filiality Emperor and temple name Huizong.

sentences.zh: 十二年八月乙酉，梓宮還臨安。

translations.literal: Year 12, eighth month, day yiyou: the coffin returned to Lin’an.
translations.idiomatic: Year 12, eighth month, yiyou: the coffin returned to Lin’an.

sentences.zh: 十月丙寅，權欑於永祐陵。

translations.literal: Tenth month, day bingyin: it was temporarily enshrined at Yongyou Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, bingyin: it was temporarily enshrined at Yongyou Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁卯，祔太廟第十一室。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, day dingmao: he was enshrined in the Ancestral Temple, eleventh shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month, dingmao: he entered the Ancestral Temple’s eleventh shrine.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月己亥，加上尊諡曰體神合道駿烈遜功聖文仁德憲慈顯孝皇帝。

translations.literal: Year 13, first month, day jihai: the honorific was augmented as Emperor of Embodying the Spirit, Harmonizing the Way, Majestic Ardor, Yielding Merit, Sagely Culture, Humaneness, Virtue, Constitution, and Manifest Filiality.
translations.idiomatic: Year 13, jihai: his honorific was lengthened with Embodying the Spirit, Harmonizing the Way, Majestic Ardor, Yielding Merit, Constitution, and Manifest Filiality.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宋中葉之禍，章、蔡首惡，趙良嗣厲階。

translations.literal: Appraisal: The calamity of mid-Song—Zhang Dun and Cai Jing were the chief villains; Zhao Liangsi opened the stairway to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal: Mid-Song’s calamity—Zhang Dun and Cai Jing were chief villains; Zhao Liangsi opened the stairway to ruin.

sentences.zh: 然哲宗之崩，徽宗未立，惇謂其輕佻不可以君於下。

translations.literal: Yet when Zhezong died and Huizong had not yet been enthroned, Dun said he was frivolous and could not rule those below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Zhezong died and Huizong was not yet enthroned, Dun said he was too frivolous to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 遼天祚之亡，張覺舉平州來歸，良嗣以為納之失信于金，必啟外侮。

translations.literal: When Liao’s Tianzuo perished, Zhang Jue offered Ping prefecture in surrender; Liangsi held that accepting him would break faith with Jin and surely invite foreign attack.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao’s Tianzuo fell, Zhang Jue offered Ping in surrender; Liangsi warned that taking him would break faith with Jin and invite attack.

sentences.zh: 使二人之計行，宋不立徽宗，不納張覺，金雖強，何釁以伐宋哉？

translations.literal: Had those two men’s plans been followed—Song would not have enthroned Huizong and would not have taken Zhang Jue—how would strong Jin have found a pretext to attack Song?
translations.idiomatic: Had those two plans been followed—no Huizong, no Zhang Jue—how would strong Jin have found a pretext to attack Song?

sentences.zh: 以是知事變之來，雖小人亦能知之，而君子有所不能制也。

translations.literal: From this one knows that when disaster comes, even petty men can foresee it, while gentlemen sometimes cannot restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when disaster comes, petty men may foresee it while gentlemen cannot always restrain it.

sentences.zh: 跡徽宗失國之由，非若晉惠之愚、孫皓之暴，亦非有曹、馬之篡奪，特恃其私智小慧，用心一偏，疏斥正士，狎近奸諛。

translations.literal: Tracing why Huizong lost the state: it was not like Jin Hui’s stupidity or Sun Hao’s cruelty, nor like Cao or Sima usurpation—he relied only on private cleverness and small wit, his mind one-sided, driving off upright men and drawing near flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing Huizong’s loss of the state: unlike Jin Hui’s stupidity or Sun Hao’s cruelty, unlike Cao or Sima usurpation—he relied on petty cleverness, a one-sided mind, driving off upright men and drawing near flatterers.

sentences.zh: 於是蔡京以獧薄巧佞之資，濟其驕奢淫佚之志。

translations.literal: Then Cai Jing, with shallow, crafty, and fawning talent, fed his proud, extravagant, and dissolute desires.
translations.idiomatic: Then Cai Jing, shallow, crafty, and fawning, fed Huizong’s proud, extravagant, dissolute desires.

sentences.zh: 溺信虛無，崇飾遊觀，困竭民力。

translations.literal: He drowned faith in emptiness, glorified tours and spectacles, and exhausted the people’s strength.
translations.idiomatic: He drowned in emptiness, glorified tours and spectacles, and exhausted the people’s strength.

sentences.zh: 君臣逸豫，相為誕謾，怠棄國政，日行無稽。

translations.literal: Ruler and ministers lived in ease, each feeding the other’s boasts, neglecting government and daily doing what had no standard.
translations.idiomatic: Ruler and ministers lived at ease, feeding one another’s boasts, neglecting government and daily doing what had no standard.

sentences.zh: 及童貫用事，又佳兵勤遠，稔禍速亂。

translations.literal: When Tong Guan held power he again prized arms and toiled at distant campaigns, heaping disaster and hastening chaos.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong Guan held power he prized arms and distant campaigns, heaping disaster and hastening chaos.

sentences.zh: 他日國破身辱，遂與石晉重貴同科，豈得諉諸數哉？

translations.literal: Later, when the state was broken and his person disgraced, he shared the verdict of Later Jin’s Chonggui—how could he blame fate?
translations.idiomatic: When the state was broken and his person disgraced, he shared Later Jin’s Chonggui’s verdict—how could he blame fate?

sentences.zh: 昔西周新造之邦，召公猶告武王以不作無益害有益，不貴異物賤用物，況宣、政之為宋，承熙、豐、紹聖椓喪之餘，而徽宗又躬蹈二事之弊乎？

translations.literal: Of old, when the newly founded Western Zhou still stood, Duke of Shao yet told King Wu not to do what was not beneficial and harmed what was beneficial, not to prize strange things and slight useful things—how much more Song under Xuanhe and Zhenghe, inheriting the ruin left by Xining, Yuanfeng, and Shaosheng, while Huizong himself trod both abuses again?
translations.idiomatic: Of old, in newly founded Western Zhou, the Duke of Shao yet told King Wu not to do what harmed the beneficial or prize strange things over useful ones—how much more Song under Xuanhe and Zhenghe, inheriting Xining, Yuanfeng, and Shaosheng’s ruin, while Huizong trod both abuses again?

sentences.zh: 自古人君玩物而喪志，縱欲而敗度，鮮不亡者，徽宗甚焉，故特著以為戒。

translations.literal: Since antiquity rulers who toyed with things and lost their purpose, who indulged desire and ruined measure, have rarely escaped ruin—Huizong did so to the extreme; therefore it is set forth especially as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity rulers who toyed with things and lost purpose, who indulged desire and ruined measure, have rarely escaped ruin—Huizong did so to the extreme; therefore it is set forth as a warning.
